name: Lean bulk

lead: A lean bulk is a bulking phase using a modest calorie surplus, often described as 250 to 500 kcal per day above maintenance, with the goal of gaining muscle while adding as little fat as possible. It is the counterpart of the dirty bulk.
On looksmaxxing forums, users commonly ask whether a lean bulk will make them look fat or bloated, and how to balance muscle gain against facial leanness.

paras: Calorie intake is set slightly above maintenance alongside progressive resistance training, with weekly weight tracking used to keep gains slow. A Grokipedia summary cites targets of about 0.25 to 0.5 kg per week and protein of 1.6 to 2.2 g/kg per day.
Slower progress and some unavoidable fat gain are the main caveats described. Early weight gain includes glycogen and water. No safety concerns specific to modest surpluses are noted in the sources.

lead: A lean bulk, also called a clean bulk or lean gaining, is a muscle-building phase that uses a small calorie surplus and resistance training to gain muscle while limiting fat gain.[1][2] It takes longer than a large-surplus approach but is described as more precise.[1]

A Grokipedia summary describes a surplus of 250 to 500 kcal per day above maintenance, protein of 1.6 to 2.2 g/kg per day, and weekly weight checks to keep gains near 0.25 to 0.5 kg per week; it also says intermediates can expect roughly 3 to 6 kg of muscle per year, while noting that some of its figures conflict.[2]

In looksmaxxing communities the term is used by people who want to add muscle without looking soft in the face. Posters ask about surplus size and whether a lean bulk will cause bloating or fat gain.[3][4]

paras: Bulking means eating in a calorie surplus to support muscle growth, and the surplus size determines how much fat accompanies the gain.[1] A clean or lean bulk keeps the surplus small and food choices controlled, which is said to take longer but be more precise.[1]
Approaches mentioned include alternating higher- and lower-calorie days and tracking calorie and macronutrient targets.[1]

One summary says moderate and large surpluses gave similar muscle gains over short periods, with less fat gain from the moderate surplus, and that early scale increases partly reflect water and glycogen.[2] It estimates a clean bulk of 74 to 80 kg would take several months, longer than a dirty bulk.[2]
No studies found specific to lean bulking as defined in forums. General research on calorie surpluses and muscle gain is summarised only secondhand in the encyclopedia sources used here.[2]

A looksmax.org user at 155 lb asked whether a 500 kcal daily surplus would let him reach 165 lb without getting "chubby", saying he looks worse if he bloats.[3] Another thread by a teenager asks which supplements to use during a summer lean bulk.[4]
Younger posters also ask whether to start a lean bulk straight after a cut, and discuss fears of regaining fat or of a slowed metabolism.[5]

lore.intro: Forum discussion centres on how to gain muscle without losing facial definition, and whether a surplus will inevitably add facial fat.[3][5]
